label: rem:time-reversal-energy-barrier
title: Time reversal requires infinite energy in the observable sector
html:
Remark. Time reversal requires infinite energy in the observable sector

The Feynman--Stueckelberg interpretation frames the positron as a backward-traveling electron. In QOU, time reversal corresponds to chirality reversal. We replace every T_{2,3} with T_{2,3}^{\sigma}. This demands infinite energy in the observable sector.

Elementary fermions (electron). The electron is the left trefoil T_{2,3}. No continuous deformation links T_{2,3} to T_{2,3}^{\sigma} (trefoil vortex chirality flip). The Jones polynomial distinguishes their connected components. In the observable sector (q \in \mathbb{R}, q \geq 1), crossing this topological barrier requires infinite energy:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\text{flip}}(e^-) =  +\infty.

No finite-energy process converts an electron into a positron. The only accessible channel is pair creation at the exceptional divisor, costing 2m_e \approx 1.022 MeV.

Composite fermions (proton, neutron). The proton is a Borromean baryon: \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H. Its antiparticle \mathfrak{p}^{\sigma} replaces every T_{2,3} with T_{2,3}^{\sigma} (chirality remark).

Topological protection applies equally:

  1. Link type invariance. The Milnor triple linking number \bar{\mu}(123) = \pm 1 distinguishes the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 from its mirror \mathcal{B}_3^{\sigma}. No Reidemeister sequence connects them.
  2. Constituent protection. Every constituent trefoil requires an infinite-energy chirality flip.
  3. Chirality-sensitive linking. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H carries linking number +1. Its mirror carries -1. Reversal requires link destruction and recreation.

Consequently:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\text{flip}}(\mathfrak{p}) =  +\infty, \qquad
  \mathfrak{E}_{\text{flip}}(\mathfrak{n}) =  +\infty.

Antiproton production requires pair creation costing 2m_p \approx 1876.5 MeV.

Beta decay is not chirality reversal. The neutron decay \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e^{\sigma} changes the crossing orientation partition (from [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}] to [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]). This R-I embedding move preserves link type and trefoil chirality. No trefoil flips.

Summary.

Particle Chirality reversal energy Pair creation threshold
Electron e^- \infty 2m_e \approx 1.022 MeV
Proton \mathfrak{p} \infty 2m_p \approx 1876.5 MeV
Neutron \mathfrak{n} \infty 2m_n \approx 1879.1 MeV
Neutrino \nu \infty \approx 0

Sending a particle backward in time corresponds to chirality reversal. The infinite energy barrier applies to all trefoil-generated particles. Pair creation alone produces time-reversed partners.
